newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: WMC uncertain over nickel smelter damage.
newsitem.headline: WMC uncertain over nickel smelter damage.

text.p: Australian mining house WMC Ltd said on Thursday it would be midday Friday at the earliest before it could fully assess the damage to its Kalgoolie, Western Australia, nickel smelter that caused the plant to close last weekend.
The smelter was forced to shut following the collapse of part of a furnace roof.
WMC has said the smelter would remain shut for about 30 days and that the possibility existed the company would be required to declare force majeure on some nickel sales.
"That's still a possibility, but it has not been the case so far," a WMC spokesman told Reuters.
A 30 day shut down would reduce nickel matte production by about 7,000-8,000 tonnes, the spokesman said.
Between July and December 1997, the smelter produced 58,651 tonnes of nickel matte, containing 39,858 tonnes of nickel metal, the spokesman said.
About 40 percent of the matte produced at the smelter is sold directly to customers, with the remaining 60 precent further processed at WMC's Kwinana refinery near Perth, he said.
